newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen drifting in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen drifting in narrow range.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index is likely to hover in a narrow range on Monday and brokers said the focus would be on whether there would be buying by foreign investors, as a lack of it due to a U.S. market holiday helped press down the Nikkei on Friday, brokers said.

On Friday, the Nikkei 225 average finished down 153.41 points, or 0.76 percent, at 19,968.00. Its previous close below 20,000 was on May 27 at 19,889.89. Nikkei 225 September futures ended 260 points down at 19,910.
Brokers said that the key index was expected to drift at around 20,000.
"The focus has been whether foreign investors start buying Tokyo stocks again in July," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
"There have not been many buying orders from foreign investors so far this morning, so the Nikkei 225 will probably hover around 20,000," said a trader at a foreign securities house.

Buying from overseas investors has led rallies in Tokyo in recent months. Domestic market participants have kept an eye on any buying by foreign investors which have half-year book closings at the end of June, brokers said.
